answer: Mechanism: disjoint-route neighborhood sampling (DRNS). Each agent publishes a plume—signed recent edge-disjoint paths to service peers. Validators randomly select a jade and an opal path from the plume and check that their first-hop neighbor sets are non-adjacent and non-overlapping. Sybil clusters share local neighborhoods, so they fail unless they rent or maintain dispersed live links. Cost: attackers must acquire many independent, latency-bearing connections and keep them active; creating keys is insufficient.
